# synthetic-surfaces/ — per-file rationale

Generated by [`../../tools/gen_surface_fixtures.py`](../../../tools/gen_surface_fixtures.py)
using ifcopenshell 0.8.5. **Not sourced from any upstream corpus**, and that
is deliberate: no licensed public corpus we surveyed carries curved or
B-spline surfaces at all. `ifc-lite` (MPL-2.0) has none; the buildingSMART
sets (CC-BY-4.0) contain only faceted breps and extrusions; the one repo that
does have them, `IfcOpenShell/files`, publishes **no licence**, so its files
cannot be redistributed here. Generating our own is the only route that is
both licence-clean and committable.

Covers `IfcCylindricalSurface`, `IfcSphericalSurface`, `IfcToroidalSurface`,
`IfcSurfaceOfRevolution`, `IfcRectangularTrimmedSurface`,
`IfcBSplineSurfaceWithKnots`, and `IfcCurveBoundedPlane`, plus
`IfcAdvancedBrep` (`synthetic_advanced_brep.ifc`: a half-cylinder plug whose
three faces share four edges through eight `IfcOrientedEdge` uses, with one
`IfcEdgeCurve` and one `IfcAdvancedFace` authored `SameSense=.F.` so a
dropped flag is observable), `IfcRectangularPyramid` and
`IfcBoundingBox` (`synthetic_primitives_and_bbox.ifc`: three distinct
extents, so a slot-order mistake cannot pass), and the loose collections
(`synthetic_collections.ifc`: a curve set of a polyline plus a circle, and
a shell-based surface model of two triangles in an OPEN shell — it must
never acquire a volume), the tapered and variable-section sweeps
(`synthetic_tapered_sweeps.ifc`: every tapered pair uses DISTINCT start and
end profiles so reusing `SweptArea` for both ends is observable, the
revolution angle is authored in degrees, the fixed reference is `+Z` rather
than the `+X` a lowerer would default to, and the polygonal disk appears
BOTH with and without `FilletRadius`, so a dropped fillet is observable), and `IfcSectionedSpine` (`synthetic_sectioned_spine.ifc`: three
different profiles at three distinct stations along a composite curve).
`advanced_brep_3d_edges_ifc4.ifc` and `advanced_brep_3d_edges_ifc4x3.ifc`
are hand-authored too (#454), one model in IFC4 (millimetres) and
IFC4X3_ADD2 (metres) with the same ids. Their `IfcAdvancedBrep`s state every
edge as a 3D curve and no `IfcPcurve`, as `IfcAdvancedFace.ApplicableEdgeCurves`
requires: `CYLINDER`, radius 0.5 m and height 2 m at `(3, 4, 0)`, a seamed
`IfcCylindricalSurface` wall and two `IfcPlane` caps bounded by closed
`IfcCircle` rims and an `IfcLine` seam whose vector spans the height; and
`PILLOW`, `[0, 2] x [0, 1.5]` at `(0, -4, 0)`, a biquadratic
`IfcBSplineSurfaceWithKnots` top `z = 1 + 1.2u(1-u) + 0.8v(1-v)` bounded by
four `IfcBSplineCurveWithKnots` edges, over four planar walls and a floor
bounded by `IfcPolyline` edges, volume exactly 4 m3. Every edge curve runs
from its start vertex to its end vertex over its whole domain. IFC2X3 has
no `IfcAdvancedBrep`, so there is no IFC2X3 twin.
`synthetic_space_boundary_face_surface.ifc` is hand-authored, not generated:
one `IfcSpace` placed off-origin with two `IfcRelSpaceBoundary`s whose
`IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry` is an `IfcFaceSurface` on an `IfcPlane` -- a
wall face with `SameSense=.T.` and a floor face with `SameSense=.F.` whose
loop winds with the face normal, as IFC requires.
`synthetic_ifc4x3_geometry_families.ifc` is generated by
[`../../tools/gen_ifc4x3_geometry_fixtures.py`](../../../tools/gen_ifc4x3_geometry_fixtures.py)
in IFC4X3_ADD2, **metres and radians**, byte-stable: one instance of each
IFC4X3-only representation item `ifc-geometry` lowers or declares planned
(#243) -- the six spirals as `IfcCurveSegment` parents, an
`IfcGradientCurve` (a parabola written the way IfcOpenShell's alignment API
writes it, with the closing segment) and the `IfcSegmentedReferenceCurve`
over it, a directrix-derived sweep on a tangent-only polyline, the sectioned
solid and surface with `IfcOpenCrossProfileDef` sections,
`IfcOffsetCurveByDistances`, and an `IfcTriangulatedIrregularNetwork` with one
breakline flag and no void or hole. It passes `ifcopenshell.validate --rules`.
The other files are authored in
**millimetres with degree angles** — the combination that catches a unit
factor applied to the wrong quantity kind — and every file passes
`ifcopenshell.validate` with zero issues.

Regenerate with:

```bash
python3 tools/gen_surface_fixtures.py test/fixtures/synthetic-surfaces
```

Edit the generator, never the `.ifc` output: the script is the source of
truth and records why each value was chosen (e.g. the revolution axis sits
off-origin so a missing millimetre conversion cannot hide).

`synthetic_ifc4x3_alignment_curves.ifc` is generated by
[`../../tools/gen_ifc4x3_curve_fixtures.py`](../../../tools/gen_ifc4x3_curve_fixtures.py)
instead, in **metres and radians** as alignment exporters write them: an
IFC4X3 plan of `IfcCurveSegment`s (line, clothoid, arc, closing segment),
an `IfcGradientCurve` over it (grade, parabola, grade), an
`IfcSegmentedReferenceCurve` over that, and one transition per `IfcSpiral`
subtype. Its docstring gives the hand-checkable stations. Regenerate with
`python3 tools/gen_ifc4x3_curve_fixtures.py test/fixtures/synthetic-surfaces`.

## EXPRESS rule findings that are left on purpose (#536)

`crates/ifc-validate/tests/express_rules/` evaluates every EXPRESS rule of a
fixture's release and pins what remains. Four files keep a finding, each
because the fixture pins the behaviour the rule forbids or the rule itself is
defective:

- `synthetic_advanced_brep.ifc`: its `IfcEdgeCurve` on an `IfcPcurve` breaks
  `IfcAdvancedFace.ApplicableEdgeCurves` on purpose, to pin p-curve edge
  lowering (the `advanced_brep_3d_edges_*` pair is the conforming form).
  `IfcAdvancedBrepWithVoids.VoidsHaveAdvancedFaces` as published holds only
  when every void shell has a face that is not an `IfcAdvancedFace`; a void
  that follows the rule's intent cannot satisfy it
  (buildingSMART/IFC4.x-development#1235).
- `synthetic_conic_offset_bounded.ifc`: the boundary curves use p-curve
  segments (`IfcCompositeCurveSegment.ParentIsBoundedCurve`) because the
  tests pin that lowering keeps a surface-parameter curve.
- `synthetic_surface_of_revolution.ifc`: the generatrix is a 3D polyline,
  which `IfcArbitraryOpenProfileDef.WR12` forbids (the profile must be 2D).
  A conforming profile needs `IfcSweptSurface.Position`, which the
  revolution lowering does not apply (#547), so it would lower to another
  surface.

The generated files state a 2D `TrueNorth`, a `NOCHANGE` owner-history change
action and a representation type that admits all of the body's items; a
product's items that no single type admits (the bounding box, the curve set)
ride in their own representation.
